title: 〜げ
meaning: "looking ~", "seeming ~" — the outward appearance of an emotion or state.
simpleExplanation: You are judging from the outside how someone looks, so it is used mainly for other people. The result behaves as a な-adjective: 不安げな顔, 楽しげに遊ぶ.
whenUsed: Descriptive, somewhat literary writing about how a person seems.
formation: い-adj stem + げ (嬉しげ, 楽しげ, 寂しげ)
な-adj stem + げ (不安げ, 得意げ)
V-ます stem + げ (limited: 言いたげ, 自信ありげ)
Behaves as a な-adjective (〜げな N, 〜げに)

rows.label: 〜げ
cells: 彼女は寂しげに笑った

rows.label: 〜そう
cells: 彼女は寂しそうに笑った

examples.ja: 子供たちは楽しげに遊んでいる。
examples.reading: こどもたちはたのしげにあそんでいる。

examples.ja: 彼女は寂しげに窓の外を見ていた。
examples.reading: かのじょはさびしげにまどのそとをみていた。
examples.en: She was gazing out of the window, looking lonely.

examples.ja: 彼女は不安げな顔で、こちらを見た。
examples.reading: かのじょはふあんげなかおで、こちらをみた。
examples.en: She looked over at me with an anxious face.

examples.ja: 彼は何か言いたげだった。
examples.reading: かれはなにかいいたげだった。
examples.en: He looked as if he wanted to say something.

similarGrammar.difference: A quality or tendency, not the look of an emotion.

commonMistakes.why: げ describes others as seen from outside; for yourself state the feeling directly.
大人げない is a fixed negative expression.

usageNotes: Literary version of 〜そうだ (appearance). Mostly for emotions of a third person. 大人げない (childish) is a fixed exception.
Adverb form げに is the most common in narration: 寂しげに, 楽しげに, 満足げに.
jlptTips: A third person's visible emotion in a narrative passage + blank + に / な = げ.
Stem check: い-adjectives drop い (寂しげ), な-adjectives use the stem (不安げ).
Reading passages use げ to show characters' feelings; use it to answer emotion questions.
